content.text:
I changed `onCreate` in `UserResourceTypeProvider.java` so SCIM `POST /Users` always creates the user in local storage. It now calls `UserStoragePrivateUtil.userLocalStorage(session).addUser(realm, username)` instead of `UserProfile.create(false)`, which went through `session.users().addUser()` and could create the user in a federation provider. That removes the case where a successful POST returns an ID that `GET` can't find, since the read paths only query local storage. This covers the issue's minimum ask and the "always create locally" option. I did not add any federation-capability detection or a configurable strategy. I also dropped the unused `UserProfileProvider` lookup from that method. Attributes are still populated and validated through the existing recorder and profile flow after creation. I couldn't compile or run tests: an offline `mvn compile` of `scim/model` failed because the sibling snapshot artifacts (`keycloak-scim-core`, `keycloak-model-jpa`) aren't installed.

The axiomengine graph wasn't indexed, so I used grep. I didn't write any findings to the dogfood log.
